implemented_requirements.requirement: Standard 3x3 grid displayed to the users
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py creates a 3x3 matrix of tk.Button widgets inside a Frame (nested loops over BOARD_SIZE = 3).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate turns placing X or O
implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic.TicTacToe tracks current_player and switches it after each valid move; gui.py shows the current player in the status label and disables used cells.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Moves are validated (inside board, empty, game not over)
implemented_requirements.evidence: TicTacToe.is_valid_move checks bounds, emptiness, and game_over flag; make_move calls it before applying a move.
TicTacToe._check_winner scans rows, columns, both diagonals and sets winning_line and returns True.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Draw detection when board is full with no winner
implemented_requirements.evidence: make_move calls is_board_full; if true and no winner, game_over is set and winner stays None. is_draw method returns True in that case.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when a player wins or the board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: make_move sets self.game_over to True on win or on a full board; GUI checks game_over to stop further clicks.
TicTacToe.move_history records (player, row, col) for every valid move; get_move_history returns a copy.

implemented_requirements.requirement: User‑friendly interface (status display, colors, reset button)
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py provides a header, colored status label, turn indication, a "New Game" reset button, and highlights the winning line.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ability to start a new game after a round ends
implemented_requirements.evidence: Reset button calls _reset_game which invokes TicTacToe.reset() and restores button appearance and status label.

judge.summary: All core requirements for a functional, turn‑based Tic‑Tac‑Toe game with a graphical interface are present and implemented. The engine correctly validates moves, detects wins and draws, tracks history, and the Tkinter UI provides a 3x3 clickable board, turn indication, win highlighting, and a reset capability. The code appears syntactically correct and ready to run, giving a high likelihood of successful execution.
